key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile epitaxial strain jointly improve oxygen evolution activity in rare-earth nickelate thin films, with enhanced structural stability relative to LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a materials-design strategy for oxide electrocatalysts used in water electrolysis, rather than solar cells or AI.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probe defects, Ni valence, electronic structure, and electrochemical OER performance.
Use first-principles calculations to interpret strain-dependent rare-earth–oxygen–nickel hybridization.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films show earlier OER onset and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates, while the high-entropy nickelate better resists OER-induced structural degradation than LaNiO3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and transfer from epitaxial thin films to scalable electrodes remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
